- Model consistently underestimates prices, especially in early forecast periods (first 10-15 days of 30d window).
- Forecasts tend to be too low in the first 5-7 days, then gradually rise — suggesting a lag in capturing recent price momentum.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., 80+), model overreacts with excessive overshoot in the immediate forecast window.
- Model shows strong mean reversion bias — frequently forecasts prices back toward historical lows, even when true prices are trending upward.
- Forecasts for the last 5-7 days of the 30d window are often too high, suggesting overconfidence in short-term continuation of recent trends.
- Model fails to capture the “rebound” effect after sharp declines — underestimates recovery speed and magnitude.
- Forecasts for the 30d window are too optimistic in the middle of the period (days 10-20), often missing the true price dip or plateau.
